name: Shimon
overview: Shimon was a male member of the tribe of Judah, noted primarily as the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. His identity is grounded in his familial role as recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:20, with no additional personal details or notes provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Shimon appears once in the biblical record provided, with no specific meaning or divine attribution noted. It is presented simply as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shimon as the father of four sons: Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon, according to 1 Chronicles 4:20. Beyond these children, no other family relationships are documented for him.
scriptureSignificance: Shimon's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his place within the genealogy of the tribe of Judah, highlighting his role as a patriarch. Through his sons, he contributes to the lineage and tribal history preserved in the Old Testament genealogies. While details about his life are minimal, his mention affirms the continuity of the tribe of Judah's descendants.
